The manipulation of time in the story is masterfully balanced and serves its emotional core. The author uses **compression of time** effectively in the beginning to summarize five years of the narrator's childhood (from age eight to thirteen) in just a few paragraphs, quickly establishing her relationship with her father and his illness. Time is also compressed at the end, summarizing the four months leading to the father's death in a single sentence ("I won't linger there") and leaping forward decades into the narrator's adulthood to show the lasting impact of the trip. 

Conversely, the author slows the pace and **stretches time** during the most emotionally resonant moments of the seven-day cruise—specifically the first conversation with Eli by the pool and the Friday night dance with her father. By slowing down the narrative during a single three-minute song ("The Way You Look Tonight") to detail the sensory experiences, dialogue, and internal realizations, the writer gives the climax of the story the emotional weight it deserves.
